description: The British Geological Survey is the accredited MEDIN data archive centre for UK marine geology, geophysics and backscatter data, holding BGS surveys and data deposited by other organisations. Contents: geophysical data (backscatter, shallow seismic, sidescan sonar), seabed sample data from grabs and cores with geological descriptions and particle size analysis, geotechnical data, a list of marine surveys and oil and gas site survey metadata (the data themselves are held by their owners). Coverage: UK waters, including harbour approaches and nearshore areas where surveys exist. Format and access: view and download through the offshore GeoIndex, also published as a web map service, and through the deposited data search; cores can be examined at the National Geological Repository. Licence and cost: most open data are free under the Open Government Licence; data not yet prepared for online delivery may carry a charge. Caveats: coverage is uneven, and much site investigation data for specific ports and wind farms sits with private owners. Useful for seabed and subsurface conditions in port expansion, dredging and berth design and in hazard exposure studies of coastal facilities. It relates to the BGS onshore geotechnical site investigation records in the catalogue.
